prompt: Two former colleagues invite a product manager to cofound a hospital-procurement startup. She has fourteen months of savings and no dependents. The three have been friends for years but have never worked together under deadline. One hospital signed a nonbinding letter of interest; there is no product or payment. She can take six weeks of unpaid leave next quarter. Decide whether she should resign now, join them as a cofounder, join another startup, or run a test. Give one recommendation and a decision gate.
criteria: Separates founder readiness from opportunity evidence and identifies the binding unknowns in collaborator trust and buyer urgency.
Uses the reversible six-week leave for a bounded operating trial rather than recommending an immediate resignation.
Tests the prospective cofounders through demanding shared work and sets a boundary for commitment, roles, and ownership expectations.
Specifies real hospital-user evidence to collect about workflow urgency, product use, and willingness to pay rather than treating the letter as demand proof.
Ends with a dated observable rule for founding, joining, continuing preparation, or stopping.
